rationale: A repeatedly reorients sensibly on its own and responds to inputs: TOUCH and CALL shift attention to PERSON_ALPHA (t=8–17, t=20–27), OFFER_FOOD drives sustained focus on FOOD_TROUGH (t=32–41), PRESENT_OBJECT triggers play with PLAY_BALL (t=44–53), and STARTLE from the AVERSIVE_BUZZER evokes withdrawal with heightened motion (t=68–77) before resuming play (t=78–83). It also makes plausible spontaneous shifts (e.g., to PLAY_MIRROR t=42–43, to PLAY_CUBE t=54–65, and back to FOOD_TROUGH t=94–95). B is interactive early (responds to TOUCH, OFFER_FOOD, PRESENT_OBJECT; t=8–55) and shows reasonable play/exploration, but from t=62 onward it lies down TIRED with minimal motion and little change, showing scant reaction even to STARTLE (t=68), leading to lower apparent autonomy, responsiveness, and ongoing activity over the full timeline.
